candidates.title: Harry Potter (original seven-book series)
candidates.rationale: My overall choice because exceptional international reach coincides with repeated reader-vote success and a sustained culture of attachment to the same seven books. Scholastic's circulation and translation claims support scale; American, French and Polish reception supplies evidence beyond launch sales. Its chief weakness against the next two is its much shorter historical record.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Little Prince
candidates.rationale: A particularly persuasive cross-cultural contender: a French children's fable that also circulates among adults, performs well in German and Chinese reader evidence, and continues to acquire translations. The official translation milestone includes languages and varieties, rather than a clean count of distinct living languages. Longevity-weighted versions of this ranking could reasonably place it first.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Lord of the Rings
candidates.rationale: The strongest older modern-fantasy contender, combining victories in British and German favourite-book campaigns with sustained genre-reader devotion. Decades of voluntary identification with its world support the placement; adaptations reinforce an already established readership. It trails the first two only on my judgment of how broadly the books reach beyond committed fantasy readers.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Bible
candidates.attribution: Multiple authors; Jewish and Christian scriptural traditions
candidates.rationale: Repeated devotional engagement, worldwide scriptural access and a high German public-vote placement establish an extraordinary continuing relationship with this collection. American Bible Society research adds a contemporary, geographically limited engagement signal. This position compares unlike forms of attachment: religious observance and affection for a novel. Copies distributed and numbers of religious adherents are not treated as readers who love it.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Limited comparability. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Quran
candidates.attribution: Islamic scripture; traditionally revealed to Muhammad
candidates.rationale: Pew's multinational research documents frequent reading of, or listening to, the Quran in diverse Muslim societies. That continuing practice is unusually strong evidence of durable textual attachment across cultures. Its placement remains a cross-category judgment: devotional commitment cannot be converted into favourite-novel votes, and neither religious identity nor compulsory study is counted as proof of voluntary affection.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Limited comparability. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Pride and Prejudice
candidates.rationale: An unusually consistent bridge between canonical literature and popular pleasure, supported by British and American favourite-book votes and Chinese reader rankings. Repeated screen revivals and personal accounts of attachment add transmission evidence. Austen's critical standing is unnecessary to the case: the strongest argument is how repeatedly ordinary readers choose this particular novel.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Anne of Green Gables
candidates.rationale: The combination of North American and British reader voting with documented Japanese translation and reception makes this more than a Canadian national treasure. The Japanese evidence is especially valuable because it traces a sustained relationship across language and generations. This entry covers the first novel, while affection for the wider Anne sequence is supporting context.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: To Kill a Mockingbird
candidates.rationale: The winner of PBS's American favourite-book vote also has strong British, German and Chinese reader evidence and exceptional New York library circulation. This convergence distinguishes voluntary attachment from its familiar school status. Its most concentrated evidence remains American; the ranking does not assume that every assigned reader shares the affection expressed by its supporters.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Journey to the West
candidates.rationale: A central Chinese popular narrative whose characters have travelled through Asian storytelling, television and newer media, with direct Chinese reader support alongside international translation and reading discussions. That unusually long transmission history justifies a very high placement. Recognition of Monkey, however, is broader than completion of the long novel; adaptations are corroboration rather than a substitute for readership.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Winnie-the-Pooh
candidates.attribution: A. A. Milne; illustrated by E. H. Shepard
candidates.rationale: British and Hungarian favourite-book evidence provides a firmer basis than merchandise or character recognition alone. Centenary reporting and continuing visits to the landscape behind the stories show durable family attachment. The ranked work is Milne's 1926 book; affection for the wider Pooh world is considered cautiously because Disney's audience is much larger than the book-reading audience.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Hobbit
candidates.rationale: Its independent presence in British reader voting and Goodreads favourites supports a readership distinct from the larger Tolkien epic. A short, accessible adventure also offers a plausible route of family transmission into adult fantasy reading. I keep it separate from The Lord of the Rings because it is a complete earlier novel, and do not transfer the trilogy's poll victories to it.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Little Women
candidates.rationale: Repeated high placement in British and American favourite-book voting establishes a long-lived voluntary readership. Continuing adaptation, including stage renewal, adds evidence of stories and characters being passed between generations. School and canonical status help visibility, but the position rests on reader choice and sustained emotional identification rather than an assertion that all audiences respond alike.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
candidates.attribution: Lewis Carroll; illustrated by John Tenniel
candidates.rationale: British and American votes, translation scholarship, reader-group discussion and anniversary exhibitions together show a durable international life for the original book. Its distinctive imaginative language helps explain why readers revisit it at different ages. Through the Looking-Glass is a separate work and is not silently added here; some broader Alice reception necessarily concerns both books.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Ramayana
candidates.rationale: The epic has an exceptional history of family, religious and performance transmission across South and Southeast Asia. UNESCO's Ramlila record supplies concrete evidence of living communal attachment. Much of that tradition draws on Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas or other retellings, however: this entry names the Valmiki Ramayana and does not count every related performance as readership of that Sanskrit text.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Limited comparability. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Dream of the Red Chamber / The Story of the Stone
candidates.attribution: Cao Xueqin; 120-chapter edition completed/edited by Gao E and Cheng Weiyuan
candidates.rationale: Chinese reader evidence gives this a claim far stronger than its visibility in English-language lists suggests: it leads the consulted Douban ranking and has a documented culture of rereading. Its long, intricate form limits casual international penetration. The placement weights deep attachment within a very large reading tradition without pretending that one Chinese platform represents everyone in China.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Chronicles of Narnia (seven-book series)
candidates.rationale: American reader voting, British support for individual volumes and Goodreads favourites converge on an enduring children's fantasy readership. The cycle's family and school transmission makes a generational argument plausible. The seven books count once; a vote for The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe supports the cycle but is not treated as evidence that every voter read all seven.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Count of Monte Cristo
candidates.rationale: French and American public votes, Chinese reader rankings and enthusiastic independent reading accounts support this unusually durable adventure favourite. Recent adaptation reporting adds renewal evidence to a readership established long before the films. Its length does not prevent intense devotion, although a film audience rating is used only for adaptation reception and never as a rating of the novel.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
candidates.rationale: A rare literary novel with major Latin American cultural attachment, international commercial longevity and strong Chinese reader support. Reception histories and Colombian responses to adaptation help distinguish living popular ownership from Nobel prestige. The evidence also includes readers who struggle with it; its high placement recognises broad, durable devotion without claiming universal accessibility or affection.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Charlotte's Web
candidates.attribution: E. B. White; illustrated by Garth Williams
candidates.rationale: American favourite-book voting and library borrowing combine with children's reading organisations and an indexed StoryGraph account of one family reading it across generations. That small personal account illustrates transmission rather than measuring its prevalence. The resulting case joins scale to emotional attachment particularly well, although the strongest circulation evidence is from the United States.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Nineteen Eighty-Four (1984)
candidates.rationale: British, American, Hungarian and Chinese reader evidence makes this one of the most geographically convincing modern classics. Library borrowing provides another route beyond favourite-book lists. Its political recognisability matters, but I distinguish valuing and repeatedly returning to a disturbing book from finding it comforting; topical sales surges alone do not explain this placement.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Jane Eyre
candidates.rationale: Strong British and American favourite-book placements, supported by ongoing reader-platform devotion, make this a convincing case of affection surviving compulsory study. Its character-centred appeal bridges romance and literary fiction. The comparative evidence assembled here is more heavily Anglophone than for several books above it, which limits claims about an exact worldwide position.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Pippi Longstocking
candidates.attribution: Astrid Lindgren; illustrated by Ingrid Vang Nyman
candidates.rationale: Eighty-year commemorations in Swedish, Spanish-language and international settings document continuing attachment to Pippi beyond Scandinavia. Official cultural programming and reception reporting support repeated childhood transmission. This is the first Pippi novel, not Lindgren's entire output; sales attributed to the author or recognition of the character cannot all be assigned to this one book.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Diary of a Young Girl / The Diary of Anne Frank
candidates.attribution: Anne Frank; initially edited by Otto Frank
candidates.rationale: The diary's publication and translation history, anniversary reception and continuing adaptations document a remarkable international relationship with an individual voice. Its place rests on sustained personal identification as well as educational transmission. Remembrance of Anne Frank and the Holocaust is not automatically love of the diary, and readers encounter materially different edited and expanded editions.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Sherlock Holmes (Doyle's four novels and 56 stories)
candidates.rationale: Direct Chinese reader support supplements the long international history documented by the British Library. The persistence of Holmes across changing media strengthens an already established reading culture. Doyle's complete canonical stories and novels count as one defined collection; adaptations involving the character do not establish that their audiences read all sixty works.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Don Quixote
candidates.rationale: A long-lived Spanish national and international narrative that still appears in voluntary American and reader-platform selections. That reader evidence earns inclusion independently of writers calling it the greatest novel. The enormous historical sales totals often repeated online are not reliable enough for this ranking, and recognition of the knight is plainly broader than readership of both parts.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Mahabharata (including the Bhagavad Gita)
candidates.rationale: The epic and its embedded Bhagavad Gita have sustained religious reading, retelling and adaptation over an exceptionally long period. Their continuing cultural life supports a place among deeply cherished texts. Comparative evidence is weaker than the tradition's scale might imply: devotion to the Gita, knowledge of episodes and completion of the whole Mahabharata are different experiences, not additive readership totals.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Limited comparability. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Grimms' Fairy Tales / Children's and Household Tales
candidates.attribution: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm, collectors and editors
candidates.rationale: Long publication history and direct Chinese reader support demonstrate that these tales have travelled far beyond their German source community. Family retelling offers a powerful transmission mechanism. The collection is the ranked unit; modern retellings often soften or alter it, so love for Cinderella or Snow White cannot be equated with reading a particular Grimm edition.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Romance of the Three Kingdoms
candidates.rationale: Chinese reader rankings provide direct support for a narrative with centuries of historical and popular transmission. Its continuing life in East Asian adaptations helps explain durability beyond formal literary esteem. Different abridgements and media versions greatly enlarge recognition, however; their audiences are not counted as complete readers of the original novel.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Fairy Tales and Stories (collected tales)
candidates.rationale: The collected tales have direct support in the consulted Chinese ranking, an important counterweight to reliance on English-language childhood lists. Their long life as translated family stories supports a high placement. This is Andersen's defined body of fairy tales and stories, not every subsequent adaptation; individual tales are not ranked again as separate books.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Heidi
candidates.rationale: Swiss cultural documentation traces a children's novel that became an international symbol and repeatedly reached new audiences, including through Japanese animation. Its long publishing life supports genuine durability. The evidence is stronger for broad cross-cultural familiarity and childhood transmission than for comparable favourite-book polling, so the precise position is less secure than its inclusion.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Les Misérables
candidates.rationale: French public voting and British reader selection supply popular evidence alongside a long international adaptation history. The novel's emotional scale and memorable characters offer a plausible basis for persistent attachment beyond critical esteem. The musical's audience is supporting evidence of story longevity, not a count of people who have read Hugo's substantial text.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Adventures of Pinocchio
candidates.rationale: Italian cultural institutions, family visits and international reception reporting show sustained attachment to Collodi's story well beyond its original serial publication. Repeated adaptations help carry it across generations. The position discounts familiar but poorly grounded claims about its being the world's second-most-translated book and distinguishes affection for the original from affection for substantially changed screen versions.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Alchemist
candidates.rationale: German and American reader voting supports a Brazilian fable whose popularity cannot be explained by literary prestige. An Indian stage example adds cross-cultural reception context. I give its motivational appeal and long post-publication life substantial weight, while treating Coelho's own sales estimates as interested testimony and acknowledging that the book is sharply divisive.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: One Thousand and One Nights / The Arabian Nights
candidates.language: Arabic, with Persian, Indian and other roots
candidates.rationale: The collection's translation and adaptation history, together with modern reader enthusiasm, supports extraordinary narrative endurance across Arabic and many other traditions. Its changing contents make comparison especially difficult: different editions contain different stories, and famous additions are not present in every Arabic manuscript tradition. The ranked unit is the recognised collection, with that instability explicitly retained.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Limited comparability. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Gone with the Wind
candidates.rationale: Strong American and British reader voting, German selection and Chinese reader support establish enduring attachment across substantially different audiences. The placement therefore survives removal of its sales and film fame. Its racial politics and historical mythology produce serious rejection as well as devotion; recording popular affection is not endorsing the novel's representation of slavery or the American South.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Animal Farm
candidates.rationale: British reader voting and strong Goodreads and Douban presence show a durable readership beyond any single political moment. Its short, accessible narrative supports repeated introduction to new readers. School assignment and the familiar allegory increase exposure, but the stronger evidence here is voluntary selection across different reading communities rather than prescribed importance.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Kite Runner
candidates.rationale: English-language reader devotion is corroborated by Chinese platform evidence, making this more internationally convincing than many similarly successful book-club novels. Its emotional accessibility helps explain a readership persisting beyond the initial bestseller period. The author is Afghan American and the original language is English; an Afghan setting does not turn this into evidence of a Dari-language reading tradition.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Crime and Punishment
candidates.rationale: British and American reader voting plus platform favourites support a Russian classic that readers actively choose despite its demanding subject. Its moral and psychological intensity plausibly explains deep devotion. The placement rewards that repeated voluntary choice, while avoiding the assumption that its canonical standing or the sheer size of Russian literature makes it universally loved.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: And Then There Were None
candidates.rationale: Christie's international favourite-book campaign identifies this particular novel, with American voting and Chinese readers providing additional support. The Christie estate's poll and its later book page report related evidence, not independent surveys. Its durable puzzle appeal earns the placement without depending on contested lifetime sales totals or pooling all Christie novels together.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Hunger Games (original trilogy)
candidates.rationale: The original trilogy retains a striking reader-platform presence and appears in American and French favourite-book evidence. Reporting on later fan gatherings indicates attachment outlasting the original publication and film cycle. Prequels and recent awards are used only as franchise-renewal context; their sales and votes are not assigned to the three ranked novels.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Wuthering Heights
candidates.rationale: British, American and French votes, reinforced by reader-platform enthusiasm, demonstrate durable attachment to this particular novel. Its passionate following coexists with readers who dislike the characters and narrative. That division lowers any claim to universal love but does not erase the unusually persistent voluntary devotion documented across successive audiences.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
candidates.rationale: British public voting and specialist reader polls show unusually intense comic-fiction devotion over several decades. American selection adds broader corroboration. This entry is the first novel: some surveys or adaptations use the title for the wider sequence, and that ambiguity is discounted rather than resolved by crediting the first book with every franchise response.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: A Thousand Splendid Suns
candidates.rationale: Reader-platform support in English and Chinese combines with continuing book-club activity, including a documented Ukrainian discussion. That geographical spread strengthens the case beyond initial sales. The emotional response to friendship and suffering supplies a plausible attachment mechanism, while publisher claims and retailer descriptions are treated as reach evidence rather than proof that purchasers loved it.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Book Thief
candidates.rationale: A high American favourite-book placement and strong Goodreads support are joined by twentieth-anniversary editions, events and reading-group activity. Together they show persistence beyond an initial bestseller season. Its two-decade record is shorter than that of older classics, and the assembled international reception evidence remains concentrated in English-language channels.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Dune
candidates.rationale: American and British reader evidence, Goodreads support and Polish readership reporting support a durable science-fiction audience for the first novel. Later adaptations renew that audience. NPR's high placement concerns the Dune Chronicles, so it is only contextual here; no series-wide sales or poll result is silently converted into a measurement of this one volume.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Water Margin / Outlaws of the Marsh
candidates.rationale: This Chinese classic has a long popular life through storytelling, publishing and adaptations, supplemented by an account of Yu Hua's reading relationship with it. The sustained tradition warrants inclusion beyond Western visibility. Direct comparable reader polling is thinner in the assembled evidence than for the other major Chinese novels, and different-length editions complicate the unit being loved.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Secret Garden
candidates.rationale: Voluntary British reader selection and platform favourites reinforce a children's reading organisation's continuing recommendation. The book's recovery-and-belonging story offers a plausible basis for family transmission and later rediscovery. Its school and adaptation presence supports longevity, but the position does not depend on treating assigned reading or familiarity with a film as affection for the novel.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Master and Margarita
candidates.rationale: British selection and a prominent place in Hungary's favourite-book campaign support a Russian novel with a devoted international readership. Its attraction is not reducible to being a required classic. Publication after the author's death and differences between censored and fuller editions complicate reception history; the placement concerns the recognised novel across those textual forms.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Matilda
candidates.attribution: Roald Dahl; illustrated by Quentin Blake
candidates.rationale: British reader voting provides direct affection evidence, while anniversary activity from Quentin Blake and readers shows continuing attachment after thirty years. Matilda's appeal as a child reader resisting hostile adults gives family transmission a plausible basis. Recognition generated by screen and stage versions supports durability but does not measure how many audiences read the book.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Charlie and the Chocolate Factory
candidates.rationale: British favourite-book evidence and trade reporting around the fiftieth anniversary support continuing readership long after initial publication. Its imaginative wish-fulfilment and highly recognisable setting help explain repeated childhood discovery. This entry covers Charlie's first adventure, and neither Dahl's total sales nor the entire Wonka film audience is credited to it.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Very Hungry Caterpillar
candidates.rationale: Long-running library borrowing and children's reading recommendations give this picture book evidence of repeated use rather than just shelf presence. Reporting on Carle's readership adds international context. Very short books naturally generate frequent family rereading and loans, so circulation is not compared mechanically with the borrowing of thousand-page novels.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Fahrenheit 451
candidates.rationale: Genre-reader selection and unusually strong historical New York library circulation support a long-lived readership, while the NEA's community-reading programme supplies organised transmission evidence. Its political vocabulary adds recognisability. I treat the programme as a route to readers, not proof that all participants enjoy it or share one interpretation.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Things Fall Apart
candidates.rationale: African anniversary activity and reception reporting combine with international circulation history and American reader selection. This supports a living readership beyond Achebe's position in literary curricula. The balance of evidence is less globally standardised than for many English-language classics; educational importance and admiration for the author cannot by themselves establish affection for this novel.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Da Vinci Code
candidates.rationale: American public voting, Goodreads favourites and Hungarian nomination evidence show that the novel retained supporters after its enormous launch-era visibility. That persistence earns a place despite critical hostility. Its record is still much shorter than the older mysteries above it, and controversy-driven buying is treated as reach, not automatically as reader love.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Treasure Island
candidates.rationale: A Victorian adventure still attracting voluntary British favourite-book votes more than a century after publication has a credible durability claim. Its recognisable pirate world offers a route of repeated childhood transmission. The assembled comparative evidence is narrower than for the books above it, so this position rests more heavily on one national reader tradition.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Rebecca
candidates.rationale: Repeated strong British and American public-vote performance, supported by reader-platform favourites, makes this a particularly convincing durable suspense-and-romance choice. The reader evidence earns the placement independently of cinematic fame. Its strongest directly comparable support is Anglophone, which limits how precisely its international affection can be ordered against translated regional favourites.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: War and Peace
candidates.rationale: British and American favourite-book votes and continuing reader-platform selection demonstrate voluntary attachment to a notoriously substantial novel. That is stronger evidence than its frequent appearance on critics' greatest-books lists. Its fame and educational status exceed the number of complete readers; neither ownership nor name recognition is counted as proof of having read and loved it.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer
candidates.rationale: Its strong American favourite-book placement is direct evidence that this nineteenth-century childhood adventure remains actively cherished. That matters more here than Mark Twain's canonical reputation. The consulted evidence is geographically concentrated, and the novel's school presence and familiar characters are not enough to establish equivalent affection in every country where it is translated.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Old Man and the Sea
candidates.rationale: British reader voting, a Hungarian nomination and Goodreads favourites support a concise twentieth-century classic with durable voluntary readership. Its accessibility gives it a plausible route into family and school transmission. Its literary prizes and assignments are background; the place rests on readers continuing to select it rather than on the author's prestige.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: To Live
candidates.rationale: Very strong Chinese reader evidence is reinforced by accounts of Yu Hua's popularity and the book's continuing reception. This is a central example of why an English-platform ranking would miss major popular affection. Chinese depth receives substantial weight, while international recognisability and affection are less uniformly documented than the domestic case.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
candidates.rationale: American cultural-history documentation and reader-platform favourites support a book whose life extends well beyond its original publication. The relationship between book, film and childhood memory sustains the story across generations. The iconic film is not evidence that every admirer loves Baum's text, and the wider Oz sequence is excluded from this single-book entry.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Where the Wild Things Are
candidates.rationale: Historical library borrowing and continuing children's reading recommendations demonstrate use and affection across successive childhoods. Its compact imaginative story is especially suited to rereading with adults. The evidence is strongest in English-language family reading, and repeated loans of a short picture book are not interpreted as a comparable number of unique novel readers.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Great Gatsby

The assembled evidence is concentrated in one national poll, so the exact global place is uncertain; the moral importance of animal welfare is not itself treated as evidence of reader enjoyment.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Goodnight Moon
candidates.attribution: Margaret Wise Brown; illustrated by Clement Hurd
candidates.rationale: Publisher anniversary material and a reader's account of its continuing bedtime role provide evidence of durable family use. The form encourages the kind of repeated shared reading central to this ranking. The source base is largely American and partly promotional, so its familiar status is not inflated into a demonstrated worldwide favourite-book position.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Snowy Day
candidates.rationale: The historical New York Public Library checkout result is unusually strong evidence of repeated access to this picture book, and its publication history supports longevity. That result concerns one library system, not the world. The position recognises sustained childhood use while discounting the frequency advantage that a short, often reread book has over long fiction.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Robinson Crusoe
candidates.rationale: Hungarian nomination evidence and a reader's account of returning every summer support a classic with an enduring voluntary audience. Family-reader discussion also contains sharply opposed responses. That disagreement matters: the survival story's enormous recognisability is broader than affection for Defoe's full text, and cultural importance is not allowed to stand in for enjoyment.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas
candidates.rationale: Hungarian nomination and an active classics-reading discussion supply direct evidence that the original adventure still attracts readers. Modern responses also criticise its pace and descriptive passages. The ranking therefore recognises durable attachment while discounting mere familiarity with Captain Nemo, screen versions and the general reputation of Verne as a pioneer.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
candidates.rationale: American public voting and a prominent reader-platform presence demonstrate a continuing constituency for Wilde's novel beyond quotations and classroom study. Its compact premise supports repeated discovery by different reading generations. The original magazine and revised book versions are treated as one work; the author's cultural visibility is not a substitute for title-specific affection.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Frankenstein
candidates.rationale: American favourite-book selection and reader-platform votes establish attachment to the novel itself. Its long adaptation life strengthens recognisability but can obscure major differences from the source. The placement deliberately gives more weight to book-reader choice than to the ubiquitous screen image of the creature, and treats the 1818 and 1831 texts as versions of one work.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Dracula
candidates.rationale: British reader selection and platform favourites support a lasting readership for the original novel. Its influence on horror and constant adaptation provide transmission routes but are not enough alone. Vampire fandom is much wider than affection for Stoker's epistolary text; the ranking keeps those audiences conceptually separate.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Thorn Birds
candidates.rationale: British favourite-book evidence, publication history and independent rereading responses support a romance-and-family saga surviving well beyond its original bestseller period. The famous television adaptation supplies context for transmission. Its strongest record remains within English-language popular reading, so the position is more cautious than a ranking based simply on historical sales would be.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Time Traveler's Wife
candidates.rationale: Reader-platform support, a book-club discussion and the author's foreign-edition record establish affection beyond the original American launch. The assembled responses include strong dislike as well as devotion. A new collector's edition and sequel announcement show continued interest, but affection for an unpublished sequel is not inferred and adaptation audiences are not counted as readers.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Notebook
candidates.rationale: American public voting and reader-platform favourites identify a durable romantic readership for the novel. That direct support earns inclusion independently of the film's visibility. Its sentimental appeal is also divisive, and the evidence is concentrated in English-language popular reading; neither Sparks's career-wide sales nor film viewers are assigned to this single book.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Catch-22
candidates.rationale: British and American favourite-book voting establishes persistent voluntary attachment to this demanding comic novel. Its cultural vocabulary adds recognisability, but the direct reader choices are the stronger evidence. A very high British placement is moderated here because the assembled international comparison is less broad than for the highest-ranked modern classics.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Yacoubian Building
candidates.rationale: Arabic-language reporting documents commercial reach and continued discussion of the novel's social world; later audiobook and adaptation material adds transmission evidence. This supports an audience beyond literary prizes. Much of the available material concerns sales and screen interpretation, so the strength of enduring book affection is less precisely established than its cultural prominence.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Season of Migration to the North
candidates.rationale: Arabic readers' saved passages and international reader testimony show continuing personal engagement with the novel. An Eritrean-born writer's recollection adds a concrete regional reading history. Critical Arabic lists are contextual rather than votes from ordinary readers; this is a more contestable inclusion because the assembled evidence of mass affection is thinner than the evidence of literary significance.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Four Reigns
candidates.rationale: Thai cultural presentation, reader reviews and historical reception reporting support a family-and-national narrative that remains a route into Thai social memory. Its regional longevity earns substantial weight. The evidence is not a representative Thai favourite-book poll, and admiration for the historical period or screen adaptations cannot by itself establish love of the complete novel.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Under the Yoke
candidates.rationale: Winning Bulgaria's national favourite-book campaign provides unusually direct evidence of public attachment, supplemented by local discussion. That is stronger than merely identifying the work as a school classic. Its international reach is narrower than its national importance, which explains a lower worldwide placement despite the exceptional strength of the Bulgarian result.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Paul Street Boys
candidates.rationale: The Hungarian favourite-book campaign and the novel's international publication and reception history support a deeply rooted childhood favourite. Its high national result is direct affection evidence rather than a proxy from assignments. The worldwide position is more cautious because Hungarian intensity and international school transmission cannot be assumed to produce equal attachment in every receiving culture.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The Good Soldier Švejk
candidates.rationale: Hungarian nomination and reporting on an international culture of restaurants named for Švejk show continuing popular ownership of the character. That unusual cultural afterlife supplements the novel's long readership. It also creates a limitation: eating at a themed restaurant or recognising the soldier is not evidence of completing or loving Hašek's unfinished prose work.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Cry, the Beloved Country
candidates.rationale: Publishing history, a major American book-club revival and an independent reader response support continuing attachment to this South African novel. Reception scholarship helps distinguish original circulation from later abridged forms. The strongest numerical evidence concerns reach, so the placement remains cautious about how broadly school and book-club exposure converted into lasting affection.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: The No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency
candidates.rationale: The documented audience for the detective series and an extended reader appreciation support a durable relationship with this Botswana-set fictional world. The first novel is the ranked entry. Series-wide circulation and love for later instalments are only contextual; the author is Scottish, and an African setting is not labelled as African-language authorship.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Long Walk to Freedom
candidates.rationale: The autobiography's international publishing life, continuing reporting and an authorised children's adaptation show a narrative transmitted beyond its initial political moment. That is relevant reach and family-transmission evidence. Admiration for Mandela is not automatically affection for this book, and the assembled material establishes reader love less directly than it establishes fame and continued circulation.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Please Look After Mom / Please Look After Mother
candidates.rationale: Korean reporting, publisher circulation claims and a continuing international book-club discussion establish a readership extending beyond the original Korean bestseller period. An independent negative review prevents the evidence from becoming a collection of promotional praise. Its record is shorter than that of older family novels, and the comparison remains affected by uneven translation access.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Strong. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Gunahon Ka Devta
candidates.rationale: Publication and reception context is strengthened by an Indian reader discussion contrasting a parent's powerful attachment with a child's less enthusiastic response. That is concrete evidence of generational transmission and disagreement. The case is strongest within Hindi reading culture, while international comparisons are thin; regional devotion receives weight without being declared universal.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: Captains of the Sands
candidates.rationale: The documented Brazilian publication and reception history supports a long-running popular audience for this novel about marginalised young people. Its mass circulation is relevant but not sufficient by itself. The source base here is relatively narrow, so this boundary placement is less secure than the work's recognised national prominence and could move substantially with better reader evidence.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.

candidates.title: So Long a Letter
candidates.rationale: Reader-platform reception, a library-oriented international reading initiative and a personal reading response support attachment to this Senegalese novel beyond critical esteem. Reception scholarship traces its continuing place in women's writing and education. The case for mass affection is less well quantified than its cultural importance, making this an explicitly contestable final inclusion rather than a definitive exclusion of all alternatives.
candidates.caveat: Evidence assessment in the supplied report: Moderate. This is an editorial synthesis of reception, not a representative global survey or a precise vote total.
